fields.label: Layer height
fields.tip: Slicing height for each layer. Smaller layer height means more accurate and more printing time

fields.label: Initial layer height
fields.tip: Height of initial layer. Making initial layer height to be thick slightly can improve build plate adhension

fields.label: Mixed color sublayer
fields.tip: Enable splitting each mixed-filament layer into sub-layers for physical colour blending. Requires at least one enabled mixed filament row.

fields.label: Minimum mixed sublayer thickness
fields.tip: Minimum thickness of each mixed or gradient filament sublayer. Color ratios are adjusted when necessary while preserving the total layer height. Slicing stops with an error if the layer is too thin to fit all colors. Set to 0 to disable this limit.

fields.label: Default
fields.tip: Default line width if other line widths are set to 0. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

fields.label: Initial layer
fields.tip: Line width of initial layer. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

fields.label: Outer wall
fields.tip: Line width of outer wall. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

fields.label: Inner wall
fields.tip: Line width of inner wall. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

fields.label: Top surface
fields.tip: Line width for top surfaces. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

fields.label: Sparse infill
fields.tip: Line width of internal sparse infill. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

fields.label: Internal solid infill
fields.tip: Line width of internal solid infill. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

fields.label: Support
fields.tip: Line width of support. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

fields.label: Seam position
fields.tip: The start position to print each part of outer wall

fields.label: Staggered inner seams
fields.tip: This option causes the inner seams to be shifted backwards based on their depth, forming a zigzag pattern.

fields.label: Seam gap
fields.tip: In order to reduce the visibility of the seam in a closed loop extrusion, the loop is interrupted and shortened by a specified amount. This amount can be specified in millimeters or as a percentage of the current extruder diameter. The default value for this parameter is 10%.

fields.label: Scarf joint seam (beta)
fields.tip: Use scarf joint to minimize seam visibility and increase seam strength.

fields.label: Conditional scarf joint
fields.tip: Apply scarf joints only to smooth perimeters where traditional seams do not conceal the seams at sharp corners effectively.

fields.label: Conditional angle threshold
fields.tip: This option sets the threshold angle for applying a conditional scarf joint seam. If the maximum angle within the perimeter loop exceeds this value (indicating the absence of sharp corners), a scarf joint seam will be used. The default value is 155°.

fields.label: Conditional overhang threshold
fields.tip: This option determines the overhang threshold for the application of scarf joint seams. If the unsupported portion of the perimeter is less than this threshold, scarf joint seams will be applied. The default threshold is set at 40% of the external wall's width. Due to performance considerations, the degree of overhang is estimated.

fields.label: Scarf joint speed
fields.tip: This option sets the printing speed for scarf joints. It is recommended to print scarf joints at a slow speed (less than 100 mm/s). It's also advisable to enable 'Extrusion rate smoothing' if the set speed varies significantly from the speed of the outer or inner walls. If the speed specified here is higher than the speed of the outer or inner walls, the printer will default to the slower of the t

fields.label: Scarf start height
fields.tip: Start height of the scarf. This amount can be specified in millimeters or as a percentage of the current layer height. The default value for this parameter is 0.

fields.label: Scarf around entire wall
fields.tip: The scarf extends to the entire length of the wall.

fields.label: Scarf length
fields.tip: Length of the scarf. Setting this parameter to zero effectively disables the scarf.

fields.label: Scarf steps
fields.tip: Minimum number of segments of each scarf.

fields.label: Scarf joint for inner walls
fields.tip: Use scarf joint for inner walls as well.

fields.label: Role base wipe speed
fields.tip: The wipe speed is determined by the speed of the current extrusion role.e.g. if a wipe action is executed immediately following an outer wall extrusion, the speed of the outer wall extrusion will be utilized for the wipe action.

fields.label: Wipe speed
fields.tip: The wipe speed is determined by the speed setting specified in this configuration.If the value is expressed as a percentage (e.g. 80%), it will be calculated based on the travel speed setting above.The default value for this parameter is 80%

fields.label: Wipe on loops
fields.tip: To minimize the visibility of the seam in a closed loop extrusion, a small inward movement is executed before the extruder leaves the loop.

fields.label: Wipe before external loop
fields.tip: To minimise visibility of potential overextrusion at the start of an external perimeter when printing with Outer/Inner or Inner/Outer/Inner wall print order, the deretraction is performed slightly on the inside from the start of the external perimeter. That way any potential over extrusion is hidden from the outside surface. This is useful when printing with Outer/Inner or Inner/Outer/Inner wall p

fields.label: Slice gap closing radius
fields.tip: Cracks smaller than 2x gap closing radius are being filled during the triangle mesh slicing. The gap closing operation may reduce the final print resolution, therefore it is advisable to keep the value reasonably low.

fields.label: Resolution
fields.tip: G-code path is genereated after simplifing the contour of model to avoid too much points and gcode lines in gcode file. Smaller value means higher resolution and more time to slice

fields.label: Arc fitting
fields.tip: Enable this to get a G-code file which has G2 and G3 moves. The fitting tolerance is same as the resolution.

fields.label: X-Y hole compensation
fields.tip: Holes of object will be grown or shrunk in XY plane by the configured value. Positive value makes holes bigger. Negative value makes holes smaller. This function is used to adjust size slightly when the object has assembling issue

fields.label: X-Y contour compensation
fields.tip: Contour of object will be grown or shrunk in XY plane by the configured value. Positive value makes contour bigger. Negative value makes contour smaller. This function is used to adjust size slightly when the object has assembling issue

fields.label: Elephant foot compensation
fields.tip: Shrink the initial layer on build plate to compensate for elephant foot effect

fields.label: Elephant foot compensation layers
fields.tip: The number of layers on which the elephant foot compensation will be active. The first layer will be shrunk by the elephant foot compensation value, then the next layers will be linearly shrunk less, up to the layer indicated by this value.

fields.label: Precise wall
fields.tip: Improve shell precision by adjusting outer wall spacing. This also improves layer consistency. Note: This setting will only take effect if the wall sequence is configured to Inner-Outer

fields.label: Convert holes to polyholes
fields.tip: Search for almost-circular holes that span more than one layer and convert the geometry to polyholes. Use the nozzle size and the (biggest) diameter to compute the polyhole. See http://hydraraptor.blogspot.com/2011/02/polyholes.html

fields.label: Polyhole detection margin
fields.tip: Maximum defection of a point to the estimated radius of the circle. As cylinders are often exported as triangles of varying size, points may not be on the circle circumference. This setting allows you some leway to broaden the detection. In mm or in % of the radius.

fields.label: Polyhole twist
fields.tip: Rotate the polyhole every layer.

fields.label: Precise Z height
fields.tip: Enable this to get precise z height of object after slicing. It will get the precise object height by fine-tuning the layer heights of the last few layers. Note that this is an experimental parameter.

fields.label: Enable Z-layer anti-aliasing
fields.tip: Consider enabling Z-layer anti-aliasing for models with large, gently sloped surfaces to reduce visible stair-stepping. For the best possible surface finish, consider using concentric top-surface fill. When enabled, eligible top-surface and wall paths adjust their Z height to follow the model surface. Z-layer anti-aliasing is mutually exclusive with Spiral vase, Scarf joint seam, and Mixed color s

fields.label: Minimum surface slope for wall lowering
fields.tip: Sets the minimum slope for additional wall lowering, applied only to paths that pass the Z-layer anti-aliasing filter. The eligible slope range varies with layer height. Values that are too high may have no effect. Set to 0 to disable this compensation. For example, with a 0.20 mm layer height and a 0.42 mm outer-wall line width, values of 35° or higher generally produce no additional lowering. Th

fields.label: ZAA slice-plane offset
fields.tip: Sets the Z offset of the slicing plane relative to the bottom of each layer, affecting the dynamic layer thickness. When set to 0, the system automatically selects a suitable offset based on the layer height, including adaptive layer heights. The first layer is always sliced at its midplane. A larger value allows less downward adjustment and more upward adjustment of paths, increasing the risk of

fields.label: Lock top-surface fill direction
fields.tip: Keeps the direction of non-bridge, line-based top-surface fill patterns (such as Rectilinear and Monotonic) unchanged between layers when Z-layer anti-aliasing is active for the current object. Bridge fill direction and other fill types are unaffected.

fields.label: Ironing Type
fields.tip: Ironing is using small flow to print on same height of surface again to make flat surface more smooth. This setting controls which layer being ironed

fields.label: Ironing Pattern
fields.tip: The pattern that will be used when ironing

fields.label: Ironing speed
fields.tip: Print speed of ironing lines

fields.label: Ironing flow
fields.tip: The amount of material to extrude during ironing. Relative to flow of normal layer height. Too high value results in overextrusion on the surface

fields.label: Ironing line spacing
fields.tip: The distance between the lines of ironing

fields.label: Ironing angle
fields.tip: The angle ironing is done at. A negative number disables this function and uses the default method.

fields.label: Wall generator
fields.tip: Classic wall generator produces walls with constant extrusion width and for very thin areas is used gap-fill. Arachne engine produces walls with variable extrusion width

fields.label: Wall transitioning threshold angle
fields.tip: When to create transitions between even and odd numbers of walls. A wedge shape with an angle greater than this setting will not have transitions and no walls will be printed in the center to fill the remaining space. Reducing this setting reduces the number and length of these center walls, but may leave gaps or overextrude

fields.label: Wall transitioning filter margin
fields.tip: Prevent transitioning back and forth between one extra wall and one less. This margin extends the range of extrusion widths which follow to [Minimum wall width - margin, 2 * Minimum wall width + margin]. Increasing this margin reduces the number of transitions, which reduces the number of extrusion starts/stops and travel time. However, large extrusion width variation can lead to under- or overext

fields.label: Wall transition length
fields.tip: When transitioning between different numbers of walls as the part becomes thinner, a certain amount of space is allotted to split or join the wall segments. It's expressed as a percentage over nozzle diameter

fields.label: Wall distribution count
fields.tip: The number of walls, counted from the center, over which the variation needs to be spread. Lower values mean that the outer walls don't change in width

fields.label: First layer minimum wall width
fields.tip: The minimum wall width that should be used for the first layer is recommended to be set to the same size as the nozzle. This adjustment is expected to enhance adhesion.

fields.label: Minimum wall width
fields.tip: Width of the wall that will replace thin features (according to the Minimum feature size) of the model. If the Minimum wall width is thinner than the thickness of the feature, the wall will become as thick as the feature itself. It's expressed as a percentage over nozzle diameter

fields.label: Minimum feature size
fields.tip: Minimum thickness of thin features. Model features that are thinner than this value will not be printed, while features thicker than the Minimum feature size will be widened to the Minimum wall width. It's expressed as a percentage over nozzle diameter

fields.label: Minimum wall length
fields.tip: Adjust this value to prevent short, unclosed walls from being printed, which could increase print time. Higher values remove more and longer walls. NOTE: Bottom and top surfaces will not be affected by this value to prevent visual gaps on the ouside of the model. Adjust 'One wall threshold' in the Advanced settings below to adjust the sensitivity of what is considered a top-surface. 'One wall thre

fields.label: Walls printing order
fields.tip: Print sequence of the internal (inner) and external (outer) walls. Use Inner/Outer for best overhangs. This is because the overhanging walls can adhere to a neighouring perimeter while printing. However, this option results in slightly reduced surface quality as the external perimeter is deformed by being squashed to the internal perimeter. Use Inner/Outer/Inner for the best external surface finis

fields.label: Print infill first
fields.tip: Order of wall/infill. When the tickbox is unchecked the walls are printed first, which works best in most cases. Printing infill first may help with extreme overhangs as the walls have the neighbouring infill to adhere to. However, the infill will slighly push out the printed walls where it is attached to them, resulting in a worse external surface finish. It can also cause the infill to shine thr

fields.label: Wall loop direction
fields.tip: The direction which the wall loops are extruded when looking down from the top. By default all walls are extruded in counter-clockwise, unless Reverse on odd is enabled. Set this to any option other than Auto will force the wall direction regardless of the Reverse on odd. This option will be disabled if sprial vase mode is enabled.

fields.label: Flow ratio
fields.tip: The material may have volumetric change after switching between molten state and crystalline state. This setting changes all extrusion flow of this filament in gcode proportionally. Recommended value range is between 0.95 and 1.05. Maybe you can tune this value to get nice flat surface when there has slight overflow or underflow

fields.label: Top surface flow ratio
fields.tip: This factor affects the amount of material for top solid infill. You can decrease it slightly to have smooth surface finish

fields.label: Bottom surface flow ratio
fields.tip: This factor affects the amount of material for bottom solid infill

fields.label: Only one wall on top surfaces
fields.tip: Use only one wall on flat top surface, to give more space to the top infill pattern

fields.label: One wall threshold
fields.tip: If a top surface has to be printed and it's partially covered by another layer, it won't be considered at a top layer where its width is below this value. This can be useful to not let the 'one perimeter on top' trigger on surface that should be covered only by perimeters. This value can be a mm or a % of the perimeter extrusion width. Warning: If enabled, artifacts can be created if you have some

fields.label: Only one wall on first layer
fields.tip: Use only one wall on first layer, to give more space to the bottom infill pattern

fields.label: Avoid crossing wall
fields.tip: Detour and avoid to travel across wall which may cause blob on surface

fields.label: Avoid crossing wall - Max detour length
fields.tip: Maximum detour distance for avoiding crossing wall. Don't detour if the detour distance is large than this value. Detour length could be specified either as an absolute value or as percentage (for example 50%) of a direct travel path. Zero to disable

fields.label: Small area flow compensation (beta)
fields.tip: Enable flow compensation for small infill areas

fields.label: Smoothing wall speed along Z(experimental)
fields.tip: Smoothing outwall speed in z direction to get better surface quality. Print time will increases. It does not work on spiral vase mode.

fields.label: Bridge flow ratio
fields.tip: Decrease this value slightly(for example 0.9) to reduce the amount of material for bridge, to improve sag

fields.label: Internal bridge flow ratio
fields.tip: This value governs the thickness of the internal bridge layer. This is the first layer over sparse infill. Decrease this value slightly (for example 0.9) to improve surface quality over sparse infill.

fields.label: Bridge density
fields.tip: Density of external bridges. 100% means solid bridge. Default is 100%.

fields.label: Thick bridges
fields.tip: If enabled, bridges are more reliable, can bridge longer distances, but may look worse. If disabled, bridges look better but are reliable just for shorter bridged distances.

fields.label: Thick internal bridges
fields.tip: If enabled, thick internal bridges will be used. It's usually recommended to have this feature turned on. However, consider turning it off if you are using large nozzles.

fields.label: Don't filter out small internal bridges (beta)
fields.tip: This option can help reducing pillowing on top surfaces in heavily slanted or curved models. By default, small internal bridges are filtered out and the internal solid infill is printed directly over the sparse infill. This works well in most cases, speeding up printing without too much compromise on top surface quality. However, in heavily slanted or curved models especially where too low sparse

fields.label: Bridge counterbore holes
fields.tip: This option creates bridges for counterbore holes, allowing them to be printed without support. Available modes include: 1. None: No bridge is created. 2. Partially Bridged: Only a part of the unsupported area will be bridged. 3. Sacrificial Layer: A full sacrificial bridge layer is created.

fields.label: Detect overhang wall
fields.tip: Detect the overhang percentage relative to line width and use different speed to print. For 100%% overhang, bridge speed is used.

fields.label: Make overhangs printable
fields.tip: Modify the geometry to print overhangs without support material.

fields.label: Make overhangs printable - Maximum angle
fields.tip: Maximum angle of overhangs to allow after making more steep overhangs printable.90° will not change the model at all and allow any overhang, while 0 will replace all overhangs with conical material.

fields.label: Make overhangs printable - Hole area
fields.tip: Maximum area of a hole in the base of the model before it's filled by conical material.A value of 0 will fill all the holes in the model base.

fields.label: Extra perimeters on overhangs
fields.tip: Create additional perimeter paths over steep overhangs and areas where bridges cannot be anchored.

fields.label: Reverse on odd
fields.tip: Extrude perimeters that have a part over an overhang in the reverse direction on odd layers. This alternating pattern can drastically improve steep overhangs. This setting can also help reduce part warping due to the reduction of stresses in the part walls.

fields.label: Reverse only internal perimeters
fields.tip: Apply the reverse perimeters logic only on internal perimeters. This setting greatly reduces part stresses as they are now distributed in alternating directions. This should reduce part warping while also maintaining external wall quality. This feature can be very useful for warp prone material, like ABS/ASA, and also for elastic filaments, like TPU and Silk PLA. It can also help reduce warping on

fields.label: Reverse threshold
fields.tip: Number of mm the overhang need to be for the reversal to be considered useful. Can be a % of the perimeter width. Value 0 enables reversal on every odd layers regardless.

fields.label: Overhang Optimization(Beta)
fields.tip: Adaptive height and line width for each layer.

fields.label: Wall loops
fields.tip: Number of walls of every layer

fields.label: Embedding the wall into the infill
fields.tip: Embedding the wall into parts where the wall loops are absent ensures that the wall connects seamlessly to the infill.

fields.label: Alternate extra wall
fields.tip: This setting adds an extra wall to every other layer. This way the infill gets wedged vertically between the walls, resulting in stronger prints. When this option is enabled, the ensure vertical shell thickness option needs to be disabled. Using lightning infill together with this option is not recommended as there is limited infill to anchor the extra perimeters to.

fields.label: Detect thin wall
fields.tip: Detect thin wall which can't contain two line width. And use single line to print. Maybe printed not very well, because it's not closed loop

fields.label: Top surface pattern
fields.tip: Line pattern of top surface infill

fields.label: Top shell layers
fields.tip: This is the number of solid layers of top shell, including the top surface layer. When the thickness calculated by this value is thinner than top shell thickness, the top shell layers will be increased

fields.label: Top shell thickness
fields.tip: The number of top solid layers is increased when slicing if the thickness calculated by top shell layers is thinner than this value. This can avoid having too thin shell when layer height is small. 0 means that this setting is disabled and thickness of top shell is absolutely determained by top shell layers

fields.label: Bottom surface pattern
fields.tip: Line pattern of bottom surface infill, not bridge infill

fields.label: Bottom shell layers
fields.tip: This is the number of solid layers of bottom shell, including the bottom surface layer. When the thickness calculated by this value is thinner than bottom shell thickness, the bottom shell layers will be increased

fields.label: Bottom shell thickness
fields.tip: The number of bottom solid layers is increased when slicing if the thickness calculated by bottom shell layers is thinner than this value. This can avoid having too thin shell when layer height is small. 0 means that this setting is disabled and thickness of bottom shell is absolutely determained by bottom shell layers

fields.label: Top/Bottom solid infill/wall overlap
fields.tip: Top solid infill area is enlarged slightly to overlap with wall for better bonding and to minimize the appearance of pinholes where the top infill meets the walls. A value of 25-30% is a good starting point, minimising the appearance of pinholes. The percentage value is relative to line width of sparse infill

fields.label: Sparse infill density
fields.tip: Density of internal sparse infill, 100% turns all sparse infill into solid infill and internal solid infill pattern will be used

fields.label: Start sparse infill density
fields.tip: Start sparse infill density in range(1-99)

fields.label: End sparse infill density
fields.tip: End sparse infill density in range(1-99)

fields.label: Gradual direction
fields.tip: Gradual direction

fields.label: Interior coefficient (beta)
fields.tip: Controls field infill density inside the model. Higher values make the internal lattice denser.

fields.label: Surface coefficient (beta)
fields.tip: Controls field infill density near surfaces. Higher values make surface-adjacent lattice denser.

fields.label: Cell type
fields.tip: Selects the base cell shape used by field infill.

fields.label: Intelligent Infill
fields.tip: Active the Intelligent Infill On the basis of the original sparse filling.

fields.label: Sparse infill pattern
fields.tip: Line pattern for internal sparse infill

fields.label: Sparse infill anchor length
fields.tip: Connect an infill line to an internal perimeter with a short segment of an additional perimeter. If expressed as percentage (example: 15%) it is calculated over infill extrusion width. Creality Print tries to connect two close infill lines to a short perimeter segment. If no such perimeter segment shorter than infill_anchor_max is found, the infill line is connected to a perimeter segment at just

fields.label: Maximum length of the infill anchor
fields.tip: Connect an infill line to an internal perimeter with a short segment of an additional perimeter. If expressed as percentage (example: 15%) it is calculated over infill extrusion width. Creality Print tries to connect two close infill lines to a short perimeter segment. If no such perimeter segment shorter than this parameter is found, the infill line is connected to a perimeter segment at just one

fields.label: Internal solid infill pattern
fields.tip: Line pattern of internal solid infill. if the detect narrow internal solid infill be enabled, the concentric pattern will be used for the small area.

fields.label: Apply gap fill
fields.tip: Enables gap fill for the selected surfaces. The minimum gap length that will be filled can be controlled from the filter out tiny gaps option below. Options: 1. Everywhere: Applies gap fill to top, bottom and internal solid surfaces 2. Top and Bottom surfaces: Applies gap fill to top and bottom surfaces only 3. Nowhere: Disables gap fill

fields.label: Filter out tiny gaps
fields.tip: Filter out gaps smaller than the threshold specified

fields.label: Infill/Wall overlap
fields.tip: Infill area is enlarged slightly to overlap with wall for better bonding. The percentage value is relative to line width of sparse infill. Set this value to ~10-15% to minimize potential over extrusion and accumulation of material resulting in rough top surfaces.

fields.label: Anchor solid infill by X mm
fields.tip: This parameter grows the top/bottom/solid layers by the specified mm to anchor them into the sparse infill and support the perimeters above. Put 0 to deactivate it. Can be a %% of the width of the perimeters.

fields.label: Fill Multiline
fields.tip: Using multiple lines for the infill pattern, if supported by infill pattern.

fields.label: Skin infill pattern
fields.tip: Line pattern for skin

fields.label: Skeleton infill pattern
fields.tip: Line pattern for skeleton

fields.label: Skin infill density
fields.tip: The portion of the model's outer surface within a certain depth range is called the skin. This parameter is used to adjust the density of this section.When two regions have the same sparse infill settings but different skin densities, This area will not be split into two separate regions.default is as same as infill density.

fields.label: Skeleton infill density
fields.tip: The remaining part of the model contour after removing a certain depth from the surface is called the skeleton. This parameter is used to adjust the density of this section.When two regions have the same sparse infill settings but different skeleton densities, their skeleton areas will develop overlapping sections.default is as same as infill density.

fields.label: Minimum skeleton infill density
fields.tip: Minimum skeleton infill density when the prime tower is disabled. The slicer may increase the actual skeleton infill density to accommodate flushing volume. When automatic density planning is inactive, this value is used as the skeleton infill density.

fields.label: Infill lock depth
fields.tip: The parameter sets the overlapping depth between the interior and skin.

fields.label: Skin infill depth
fields.tip: The parameter sets the depth of skin.

fields.label: Skin line width
fields.tip: Adjust the line width of the selected skin paths.

fields.label: Skeleton line width
fields.tip: Adjust the line width of the selected skeleton paths.

fields.label: Skeleton wipe width
fields.tip: Adjust the skeleton line width used for slowed wiping after a material change in no-prime-tower mode.

fields.label: Infill rotate step
fields.tip: This parameter adds a slight rotation to each layer of infill to create a cross texture.

fields.label: Symmetric infill y axis
fields.tip: If the model has two parts that are symmetric about the y-axis, and you want these parts to have symmetric textures, please click this option on one of the parts.

fields.label: Infill shift step
fields.tip: This parameter adds a slight displacement to each layer of infill to create a cross texture.

fields.label: Lateral lattice angle 1
fields.tip: The angle of the first set of Lateral lattice elements in the Z direction. Zero is vertical.

fields.label: Lateral lattice angle 2
fields.tip: The angle of the second set of Lateral lattice elements in the Z direction. Zero is vertical.

fields.label: Infill overhang angle
fields.tip: The angle of the infill angled lines. 60° will result in a pure honeycomb.

fields.label: Sparse infill direction
fields.tip: Angle for sparse infill pattern, which controls the start or main direction of line

fields.label: Solid infill direction
fields.tip: Angle for solid infill pattern, which controls the start or main direction of line

fields.label: Rotate solid infill direction
fields.tip: Rotate the solid infill direction by 90° for each layer.

fields.label: Bridge infill direction
fields.tip: Bridging angle override. If left to zero, the bridging angle will be calculated automatically. Otherwise the provided angle will be used for external bridges. Use 180°for zero angle.

fields.label: Minimum sparse infill threshold
fields.tip: Sparse infill area which is smaller than threshold value is replaced by internal solid infill

fields.label: Infill combination
fields.tip: Automatically Combine sparse infill of several layers to print together to reduce time. Wall is still printed with original layer height.

fields.label: Detect narrow internal solid infill
fields.tip: This option will auto detect narrow internal solid infill area. If enabled, concentric pattern will be used for the area to speed printing up. Otherwise, rectilinear pattern is used defaultly.

fields.label: Detect floating vertical shells
fields.tip: Identify floating paths in narrow internal solid infill regions above sparse infill or internal voids, and print those paths at the bridge speed. Unmarked paths, or all paths when this option is disabled, use the vertical shell speed. Requires "Detect narrow internal solid infill" to be enabled.

fields.label: Ensure vertical shell thickness
fields.tip: Add solid infill near sloping surfaces to guarantee the vertical shell thickness (top+bottom solid layers) None: No solid infill will be added anywhere. Caution: Use this option carefully if your model has sloped surfaces Critical Only: Avoid adding solid infill for walls Moderate: Add solid infill for heavily sloping surfaces only All: Add solid infill for all suitable sloping surfaces Default va

fields.label: Initial layer
fields.tip: Speed of initial layer except the solid infill part

fields.label: Initial layer infill
fields.tip: Speed of solid infill part of initial layer

fields.label: Initial layer travel speed
fields.tip: Travel speed of initial layer

fields.label: Number of slow layers
fields.tip: The first few layers are printed slower than normal. The speed is gradually increased in a linear fashion over the specified number of layers.

fields.label: Outer wall
fields.tip: Speed of outer wall which is outermost and visible. It's used to be slower than inner wall speed to get better quality.

fields.label: Inner wall
fields.tip: Speed of inner wall

fields.label: Small perimeters
fields.tip: This separate setting will affect the speed of perimeters having radius <= small_perimeter_threshold (usually holes). If expressed as percentage (for example: 80%) it will be calculated on the outer wall speed setting above. Set to zero for auto.

fields.label: Small perimeters threshold
fields.tip: This sets the threshold for small perimeter length. Default threshold is 0mm

fields.label: Sparse infill
fields.tip: Speed of internal sparse infill

fields.label: Internal solid infill
fields.tip: Speed of internal solid infill, not the top and bottom surface

fields.label: Vertical shell speed
fields.tip: Speed for narrow internal solid infill regions that overlap sparse infill or internal voids in the layer below. Requires "Detect narrow internal solid infill" to be enabled. Percentages are relative to the internal solid infill speed. When "Detect floating vertical shells" is enabled, paths identified as floating use the bridge speed instead.

fields.label: Top surface
fields.tip: Speed of top surface infill which is solid

fields.label: Gap infill
fields.tip: Speed of gap infill. Gap usually has irregular line width and should be printed more slowly

fields.label: Support
fields.tip: Speed of support

fields.label: Support interface
fields.tip: Speed of support interface

fields.label: Slow down for overhang
fields.tip: Enable this option to slow printing down for different overhang degree

fields.label: Classic mode
fields.tip: Enable this option to use classic mode

fields.label: Slow down for curled perimeters
fields.tip: Enable this option to slow printing down in areas where potential curled perimeters may exist

fields.label: External
fields.tip: Speed of bridge and completely overhang wall

fields.label: Internal
fields.tip: Speed of internal bridge. If the value is expressed as a percentage, it will be calculated based on the bridge_speed. Default value is 150%.

fields.label: Smooth speed discontinuity area (Beta)
fields.tip: Add the speed transition between discontinuity area. Note: this feature and arc fitting are mutually exclusive. Enabling either feature will ask for confirmation before turning off the other.

fields.label: Smooth coefficient
fields.tip: The smaller the number, the longer the speed transition path. 0 means not apply.

fields.label: Travel
fields.tip: Speed of travel which is faster and without extrusion

fields.label: Normal printing
fields.tip: The default acceleration of both normal printing and travel except initial layer

fields.label: Outer wall
fields.tip: Acceleration of outer walls

fields.label: Inner wall
fields.tip: Acceleration of inner walls

fields.label: Bridge
fields.tip: Acceleration of bridges. If the value is expressed as a percentage (e.g. 50%), it will be calculated based on the outer wall acceleration.

fields.label: Sparse infill
fields.tip: Acceleration of sparse infill. If the value is expressed as a percentage (e.g. 100%), it will be calculated based on the default acceleration.

fields.label: Internal solid infill
fields.tip: Acceleration of internal solid infill. If the value is expressed as a percentage (e.g. 100%), it will be calculated based on the default acceleration.

fields.label: Initial layer
fields.tip: Acceleration of initial layer. Using a lower value can improve build plate adhesive

fields.label: Top surface
fields.tip: Acceleration of top surface infill. Using a lower value may improve top surface quality

fields.label: Travel
fields.tip: Acceleration of travel moves

fields.label: Initial layer travel
fields.tip: The acceleration of travel of initial layer

fields.label: Enable accel_to_decel
fields.tip: Klipper's max_accel_to_decel will be adjusted automatically

fields.label: accel_to_decel
fields.tip: Klipper's max_accel_to_decel will be adjusted to this %% of acceleration

fields.label: Travel short distance acceleration
fields.tip: Acceleration used for short travel moves. Short travel distance is determined by the retract_before_travel setting.

fields.label: Travel short distance threshold
fields.tip: Short travel distance threshold for travel_short_distance_acceleration.

fields.label: Default
fields.tip: Default

fields.label: Outer wall
fields.tip: Jerk of outer walls

fields.label: Inner wall
fields.tip: Jerk of inner walls

fields.label: Infill
fields.tip: Jerk for infill

fields.label: Top surface
fields.tip: Jerk for top surface

fields.label: Initial layer
fields.tip: Jerk for initial layer

fields.label: Travel
fields.tip: Jerk for travel

fields.label: Extrusion rate smoothing
fields.tip: This parameter smooths out sudden extrusion rate changes that happen when the printer transitions from printing a high flow (high speed/larger width) extrusion to a lower flow (lower speed/smaller width) extrusion and vice versa. It defines the maximum rate by which the extruded volumetric flow in mm3/sec can change over time. Higher values mean higher extrusion rate changes are allowed, resulting

fields.label: Smoothing segment length
fields.tip: A lower value results in smoother extrusion rate transitions. However, this results in a significantly larger gcode file and more instructions for the printer to process. Default value of 3 works well for most cases. If your printer is stuttering, increase this value to reduce the number of adjustments made Allowed values: 0.5-5 Adjacent segments with the same output speed may be merged. Merged se

fields.label: Apply only on external features
fields.tip: Applies extrusion rate smoothing only on external perimeters and overhangs. This can help reduce artefacts due to sharp speed transitions on externally visible overhangs without impacting the print speed of features that will not be visible to the user.

fields.label: Material shortage recovery after overhang(Beta)
fields.tip: This parameter conflicts with the max_volumetric_extrusion_rate_slope and cannot be enabled at the same time. When the slicer detects that a segment of continuous low-speed extrusion has finished and the path immediately returns to normal high-speed printing, sudden changes in speed and acceleration can cause the extrusion pressure to lag behind.This may lead to temporary under-extrusion on extern

fields.label: Safe acceleration after overhang(Beta)
fields.tip: When the slicer detects the end of a continuous low-speed extrusion region such as an overhang, it will not immediately restore the normal printing acceleration.Instead, it first uses a lower and more conservative acceleration value for a short “safe recovery segment,”allowing extrusion pressure, molten material flow, and nozzle output to gradually return to a stable state.

fields.label: Safe speed after overhang(Beta)
fields.tip: When the slicer detects the end of a continuous low-speed extrusion region such as an overhang, it will not immediately restore the normal printing speed.Instead, it first uses a lower and more conservative cruise speed for a short “safe recovery segment,”allowing the printer to pass through the transition more gently before gradually returning to the normal printing speed.

fields.label: Enable support
fields.tip: Enable support generation.

fields.label: Type
fields.tip: normal(auto) and tree(auto) is used to generate support automatically. If normal(manual) or tree(manual) is selected, only support enforcers are generated

fields.label: Style
fields.tip: Style and shape of the support. For normal support, projecting the supports into a regular grid will create more stable supports (default), while snug support towers will save material and reduce object scarring. For tree support, slim and organic style will merge branches more aggressively and save a lot of material (default organic), while hybrid style will create similar structure to normal sup

fields.label: Threshold angle
fields.tip: Support will be generated for overhangs whose slope angle is below the threshold.

fields.label: On build plate only
fields.tip: Don't create support on model surface, only on build plate

fields.label: Support critical regions only
fields.tip: Only create support for critical regions including sharp tail, cantilever, etc.

fields.label: Remove small overhangs
fields.tip: Remove small overhangs that possibly need no supports.

fields.label: Raft layers
fields.tip: Object will be raised by this number of support layers. Use this function to avoid wrapping when print ABS

fields.label: Raft contact Z distance
fields.tip: Z gap between object and raft. Ignored for soluble interface

fields.label: Support/raft base
fields.tip: Filament to print support base and raft. "Default" means no specific filament for support and current filament is used

fields.label: Support/raft interface
fields.tip: Filament to print support interface. "Default" means no specific filament for support interface and current filament is used

fields.label: Avoid interface filament for base
fields.tip: Avoid using support interface filament to print support base if possible.

fields.label: Ironing Support Interface
fields.tip: Ironing is using small flow to print on same height of support interface again to make it more smooth. This setting controls whether support interface being ironed. When enabled, support interface will be extruded as solid too.

fields.label: Support Ironing Pattern
fields.tip: The pattern that will be used when ironing.

fields.label: Support Ironing flow
fields.tip: The amount of material to extrude during ironing. Relative to flow of normal support interface layer height. Too high value results in overextrusion on the surface.

fields.label: Support Ironing line spacing
fields.tip: The distance between the lines of ironing.

fields.label: Initial layer density
fields.tip: Density of the first raft or support layer

fields.label: Initial layer expansion
fields.tip: Expand the first raft or support layer to improve bed plate adhesion

fields.label: Top Z distance
fields.tip: The z gap between the top support interface and object

fields.label: Base pattern(Normal)
fields.tip: Setting for the main pattern of normal support

fields.label: Base pattern spacing
fields.tip: Spacing between support lines

fields.label: Pattern angle
fields.tip: Use this setting to rotate the support pattern on the horizontal plane.

fields.label: Top interface layers
fields.tip: Number of top interface layers

fields.label: Bottom interface layers
fields.tip: Number of bottom interface layers

fields.label: Minimum Support Contact Area
fields.tip: Lower values generate more support contact surfaces.

fields.label: Interface pattern
fields.tip: Line pattern of support interface. Default pattern for non-soluble support interface is Rectilinear, while default pattern for soluble support interface is Concentric

fields.label: Top interface spacing
fields.tip: Spacing of interface lines. Zero means solid interface

fields.label: Normal Support expansion
fields.tip: Expand (+) or shrink (-) the horizontal span of normal support

fields.label: Support/object xy distance
fields.tip: XY separation between an object and its support

fields.label: Support/object first layer gap
fields.tip: XY separation between an object and its support at the first layer.

fields.label: Support Distance Priority
fields.tip: When 'X/Y overrides Z' is selected, the horizontal distance between the model and the support structure will remain constant, but it will result in a larger Z distance. When 'Z overrides X/Y' is selected, the distance between the support and the model in the overhang area remains constant, while the support in the XY direction provides better stability for the overhang.

fields.label: Don't support bridges
fields.tip: Don't support the whole bridge area which make support very large. Bridge usually can be printing directly without support if not very long

fields.label: Max bridge length
fields.tip: Max length of bridges that don't need support. Set it to 0 if you want all bridges to be supported, and set it to a very large value if you don't want any bridges to be supported.

fields.label: Independent support layer height
fields.tip: Support layer uses layer height independent with object layer. This is to support customizing z-gap and save print time.This option will be invalid when the prime tower is enabled.

fields.label: Validation and Repair Support
fields.tip: After the base support region is generated, validate the continuity of the organic tree support contours.When enabled, additional support paths are used to repair unsupported contour segments. When disabled, organic tree supports are generated using the original extrusion path generation process.

fields.label: Tree support branch distance
fields.tip: This setting determines the distance between neighboring tree support nodes.

fields.label: Tree support branch diameter
fields.tip: This setting determines the initial diameter of support nodes.

fields.label: Tree support branch angle
fields.tip: This setting determines the maximum overhang angle that t he branches of tree support allowed to make.If the angle is increased, the branches can be printed more horizontally, allowing them to reach farther.

fields.label: Branch Diameter Angle
fields.tip: The angle of the branches' diameter as they gradually become thicker towards the bottom. An angle of 0 will cause the branches to have uniform thickness over their length. A bit of an angle can increase stability of the organic support.

fields.label: Enable
fields.tip: The wiping tower can be used to clean up the residue on the nozzle and stabilize the chamber pressure inside the nozzle, in order to avoid appearance defects when printing objects.

fields.label: Prime tower enhance type
fields.tip: Prime tower enhance type

fields.label: Width
fields.tip: Width of prime tower

fields.label: Square prime tower
fields.tip: When this option is checked, the prime tower will be as close to a square as possible, meaning its width will be fixed.

fields.label: Skip points
fields.tip: The wall of prime tower will skip the start points of wipe path

fields.label: Internal ribs
fields.tip: Enable internal ribs to increase the stability of the prime tower.

fields.label: Prime volume
fields.tip: The volume of material to prime extruder on tower.

fields.label: Bottom fill flush layers
fields.tip: When flushing into objects skeleton is enabled, force the bottom N object layers to purge on the prime tower before printing skeleton, then walls in the configured order, then skin and surface fill. This does not change bottom shell layers.

fields.label: Top fill flush layers
fields.tip: When flushing into objects skeleton is enabled, force the top N object layers to purge on the prime tower before printing skeleton, then walls in the configured order, then skin and surface fill. This does not change top shell layers.

fields.label: Skeleton wipe speed
fields.tip: When flushing into objects skeleton is enabled, set the speed for slowed skeleton paths after a material change. Percent values are calculated from the speed each skeleton path would normally use.

fields.label: Brim width
fields.tip: Brim width of prime tower, negative number means auto calculated width based on the height of prime tower.

fields.label: Prime tower rotation angle
fields.tip: Prime tower rotation angle with respect to x-axis.

fields.label: Maximal bridging distance
fields.tip: Maximal distance between supports on sparse infill sections.

fields.label: Stabilization cone apex angle
fields.tip: Angle at the apex of the cone that is used to stabilize the wipe tower. Larger angle means wider base.

fields.label: Wipe tower purge lines spacing
fields.tip: Spacing of purge lines on the wipe tower.

fields.label: Maximum wipe tower print speed
fields.tip: The maximum print speed when purging in the wipe tower and printing the wipe tower sparse layers. When purging, if the sparse infill speed or calculated speed from the filament max volumetric speed is lower, the lowest will be used instead. When printing the sparse layers, if the internal perimeter speed or calculated speed from the filament max volumetric speed is lower, the lowest will be used i

fields.label: Prime tower start ironing
fields.tip: Ironing the purge start area reduces the risk of the nozzle scraping the prime tower during subsequent printing.

fields.label: Prime tower start offset
fields.tip: Moves the start of the prime tower purge path inward along the first purge line. This keeps startup blobs inside the tower.

fields.label: Bottom corner rib length
fields.tip: Bottom side length of the square corner ribs on the square prime tower. The rib keeps its contact length with the wipe area and tapers outward to the blocks edges at the tower top. Set to 0 to use the perimeter line spacing.

fields.label: Extra flow for purging
fields.tip: Extra flow used for the purging lines on the wipe tower. This makes the purging lines thicker or narrower than they normally would be. The spacing is adjusted automatically.

fields.label: No sparse layers (beta)
fields.tip: If enabled, the wipe tower will not be printed on layers with no toolchanges. On layers with a toolchange, extruder will travel downward to print the wipe tower. User is responsible for ensuring there is no collision with the print.

fields.label: Extra interlayer wipe layers
fields.tip: Number of consecutive single-color layers that use a serpentine wipe path on the prime tower.

fields.label: Walls
fields.tip: Filament to print walls

fields.label: Infill
fields.tip: Filament to print internal sparse infill.

fields.label: Solid infill
fields.tip: Filament to print solid infill

fields.label: Wipe tower
fields.tip: The extruder to use when printing perimeter of the wipe tower. Set to 0 to use the one that is available (non-soluble would be preferred).

fields.label: Enable
fields.tip: This option will drop the temperature of the inactive extruders to prevent oozing.

fields.label: Wait for nozzle temperature after filament change
fields.tip: Enable automatic nozzle temperature waiting after filament changes during multi-nozzle printing. Requires ooze prevention to be enabled. Disabled by default. Disabling ooze prevention or this option omits this automatic wait. Temperature commands in start and custom G-code are unaffected.

fields.label: Temperature variation
fields.tip: Temperature difference to be applied when an extruder is not active. The value is not used when 'idle_temperature' in filament settings is set to non zero value.

fields.label: Preheat temperature
fields.tip: Temperature difference applied before a nozzle is activated. The advance preheat temperature is calculated as the printing temperature plus this value.

fields.label: Preheat time
fields.tip: To reduce the waiting time after tool change, Creality can preheat the next tool while the current tool is still in use. This setting specifies the time in seconds to preheat the next tool. Creality will insert a M104 command to preheat the tool in advance.

fields.label: Flush into objects' infill
fields.tip: Purging after filament change will be done inside objects' infills. This may lower the amount of waste and decrease the print time. If the walls are printed with transparent filament, the mixed color infill will be seen outside. It will not take effect, unless the prime tower is enabled.

fields.label: Flush into this object
fields.tip: This object will be used to purge the nozzle after a filament change to save filament and decrease the print time. Colours of the objects will be mixed as a result. It will not take effect, unless the prime tower is enabled.

fields.label: Flush into objects' support
fields.tip: Purging after filament change will be done inside objects' support. This may lower the amount of waste and decrease the print time. It will not take effect, unless the prime tower is enabled.

fields.label: Use beam interlocking
fields.tip: Generate interlocking beam structure at the locations where different filaments touch. This improves the adhesion between filaments, especially models printed in different materials.

fields.label: Interface shells
fields.tip: Force the generation of solid shells between adjacent materials/volumes. Useful for multi-extruder prints with translucent materials or manual soluble support material

fields.label: Interlocking depth of a segmented region
fields.tip: Interlocking depth of a segmented region. It will be ignored if "mmu_segmented_region_max_width" is zero or if "mmu_segmented_region_interlocking_depth"is bigger then "mmu_segmented_region_max_width". Zero disables this feature.

fields.label: Interlocking beam width
fields.tip: The width of the interlocking structure beams.

fields.label: Interlocking direction
fields.tip: Orientation of interlock beams.

fields.label: Interlocking beam layers
fields.tip: The height of the beams of the interlocking structure, measured in number of layers. Less layers is stronger, but more prone to defects.

fields.label: Interlocking depth
fields.tip: The distance from the boundary between filaments to generate interlocking structure, measured in cells. Too few cells will result in poor adhesion.

fields.label: Interlocking boundary avoidance
fields.tip: The distance from the outside of a model where interlocking structures will not be generated, measured in cells.

fields.label: Enable cut retraction distance override
fields.tip: Enable an object-specific override for the cut retraction distance used when switching to this object.

fields.label: Cut retraction distance override
fields.tip: Object-specific cut retraction distance used when switching to this object.

fields.label: Skirt type
fields.tip: Combined - single skirt for all objects, Per object - individual object skirt.

fields.label: Skirt loops
fields.tip: Number of loops for the skirt. Zero means disabling skirt

fields.label: Skirt minimum extrusion length
fields.tip: Minimum filament extrusion length in mm when printing the skirt. Zero means this feature is disabled. Using a non zero value is useful if the printer is set up to print without a prime line.

fields.label: Skirt distance
fields.tip: Distance from skirt to brim or object

fields.label: Skirt height
fields.tip: How many layers of skirt. Usually only one layer

fields.label: Skirt speed
fields.tip: Speed of skirt, in mm/s. Zero means use default layer extrusion speed.

fields.label: Draft shield
fields.tip: A draft shield is useful to protect an ABS or ASA print from warping and detaching from print bed due to wind draft. It is usually needed only with open frame printers, i.e. without an enclosure. Options: Enabled = skirt is as tall as the highest printed object. Limited = skirt is as tall as specified by skirt height. Note: With the draft shield active, the skirt will be printed at skirt distance

fields.label: Brim type
fields.tip: This controls the generation of the brim at outer and/or inner side of models. Auto means the brim width is analysed and calculated automatically.

fields.label: Brim width
fields.tip: Distance from model to the outermost brim line

fields.label: Brim-object gap
fields.tip: A gap between innermost brim line and object can make brim be removed more easily

fields.label: Brim ear max angle
fields.tip: Maximum angle to let a brim ear appear. If set to 0, no brim will be created. If set to ~180, brim will be created on everything but straight sections.

fields.label: Brim ear detection radius
fields.tip: The geometry will be decimated before dectecting sharp angles. This parameter indicates the minimum length of the deviation for the decimation. 0 to deactivate

fields.label: Slicing Mode
fields.tip: Use "Even-odd" for 3DLabPrint airplane models. Use "Close holes" to close all holes in the model.

fields.label: Print sequence
fields.tip: Print sequence, layer by layer or object by object

fields.label: Intra-layer order
fields.tip: Print order within a single layer

fields.label: Spiral vase
fields.tip: Spiralize smooths out the z moves of the outer contour. And turns a solid model into a single walled print with solid bottom layers. The final generated model has no seam

fields.label: Ignore inner color
fields.tip: In certain situations where color changes are unnecessary within a model, check this option to skip the color change process. This improves printing efficiency and reduces filament waste.

fields.label: Smooth Spiral
fields.tip: Smooth Spiral smoothes out X and Y moves as wellresulting in no visible seam at all, even in the XY directions on walls that are not vertical

fields.label: Max XY Smoothing
fields.tip: Maximum distance to move points in XY to try to achieve a smooth spiralIf expressed as a %, it will be computed over nozzle diameter

fields.label: Timelapse
fields.tip: If smooth or traditional mode is selected, a timelapse video will be generated for each print. After each layer is printed, a snapshot is taken with the chamber camera. All of these snapshots are composed into a timelapse video when printing completes. If smooth mode is selected, the toolhead will move to the excess chute after each layer is printed and then take a snapshot. Since the melt filamen

fields.label: Fuzzy Skin
fields.tip: Randomly jitter while printing the wall, so that the surface has a rough look. This setting controls the fuzzy position

fields.label: Fuzzy skin generator mode
fields.tip: Fuzzy skin generation mode. Works only with Arachne! Displacement: Сlassic mode when the pattern is formed by shifting the nozzle sideways from the original path. Extrusion: The mode when the pattern formed by the amount of extruded plastic. This is the fast and straight algorithm without unnecessary nozzle shake that gives a smooth pattern. But it is more useful for forming loose walls in the ent

fields.label: Fuzzy skin noise type
fields.tip: Noise type to use for fuzzy skin generation: Classic: Classic uniform random noise. Perlin: Perlin noise, which gives a more consistent texture. Billow: Similar to perlin noise, but clumpier. Ridged Multifractal: Ridged noise with sharp, jagged features. Creates marble-like textures. Voronoi: Divides the surface into voronoi cells, and displaces each one by a random amount. Creates a patchwork tex

fields.label: Fuzzy skin point distance
fields.tip: The average diatance between the random points introducded on each line segment

fields.label: Fuzzy skin thickness
fields.tip: The width within which to jitter. It's adversed to be below outer wall line width

fields.label: Fuzzy skin feature size
fields.tip: The base size of the coherent noise features, in mm. Higher values will result in larger features.

fields.label: Fuzzy Skin Noise Octaves
fields.tip: The number of octaves of coherent noise to use. Higher values increase the detail of the noise, but also increase computation time.

fields.label: Fuzzy skin noise persistence
fields.tip: The decay rate for higher octaves of the coherent noise. Lower values will result in smoother noise.

fields.label: Apply fuzzy skin to first layer
fields.tip: Whether to apply fuzzy skin on the first layer

fields.label: Reduce infill retraction
fields.tip: Don't retract when the travel is in infill area absolutely. That means the oozing can't been seen. This can reduce times of retraction for complex model and save printing time, but make slicing and G-code generating slower

fields.label: Verbose G-code
fields.tip: Enable this to get a commented G-code file, with each line explained by a descriptive text. If you print from SD card, the additional weight of the file could make your firmware slow down.

fields.label: Label objects
fields.tip: Enable this to add comments into the G-Code labeling print moves with what object they belong to, which is useful for the Octoprint CancelObject plugin. This settings is NOT compatible with Single Extruder Multi Material setup and Wipe into Object / Wipe into Infill.

fields.label: Exclude objects
fields.tip: Enable this option to add EXCLUDE OBJECT command in g-code
